title: The Arithmetic of Scarcity
sentences: Being short of money is very often described as a straightforward failure of discipline.
The more careful explanations point somewhere considerably less comfortable than that.
Scarcity consumes attention, and attention is precisely what good decisions require.
Someone calculating whether they can afford the bus fare is not being careless with money.
They are running a computation that wealthier people are never obliged to run at all.
The same mind, given a little more room to work in, tends to make noticeably better choices.
This reverses the usual direction of the moral story that we tell ourselves about poverty.
Poor decisions are frequently a symptom of the condition rather than the cause of it.
Policies built on the older story tend to add further conditions and more paperwork.
Each condition consumes precisely the resource that was already exhausted to begin with.
